cant-trust-the-news.name: Trust in news
cant-trust-the-news.line: I don't trust the news to tell me the whole story fairly.

sources.passage: Americans’ confidence in the mass media has edged down to a new low, with just 28% expressing a “great deal” or “fair amount” of trust in newspapers, television and radio to report the news fully, accurately and fairly. This is down from 31% last year and 40% five years ago . Meanwhile, seven in 10 U.S. adults now say they have “not very much” confidence (36%) or “none at all” (34%).
overall trust in the news (40%) has remained stable for the third year in a row, even if it is still four points lower overall than it was at the height of the Coronavirus pandemic

cant-trust-the-news.prevalence: 28% of Americans trusted newspapers, television and radio to report the news fully, accurately and fairly, down from 40% five years ago; seven in 10 had not very much (36%) or no (34%) confidence (Gallup). Across markets, trust in the news stands at 40% (Reuters Institute Digital News Report).

news-overload.name: News overload
news-overload.line: The news wears me down, so I've started tuning it out.

sources.passage: Across markets, four in ten (40%) say they sometimes or often avoid the news, up from 29% in 2017 and the joint highest figure we’ve ever recorded (along with 2024).
selective avoiders who struggle with news overload and look to protect themselves at certain times or for particular topics

news-overload.prevalence: Across markets, 40% sometimes or often avoid the news, up from 29% in 2017 (Reuters Institute Digital News Report).

ai-fakes.name: AI fakes
ai-fakes.line: I can't tell if a photo, video or voice is real or made by AI.

sources.passage: most Americans (76%) say it’s extremely or very important to be able to tell if pictures, videos and text were made by AI or people. But 53% of Americans are not too or not at all confident they can detect if something is made by AI versus a person.

ai-fakes.prevalence: 76% of Americans say being able to tell AI-made content from human-made content is extremely or very important, but 53% are not confident they can (Pew Research Center).

data-leaks.name: Data leaks
data-leaks.line: My personal information keeps leaking out through hacks and data breaches.

sources.passage: Data compromise incidents hit a record of 3,322 in 2025, with 70 percent of related breach notices failing to explain how the breach happened, according to a new report from the Identity Theft Resource Center (ITRC).

And 11% have had their email or social media accounts taken over without permission, while 7% have had someone attempt to open a line of credit or apply for a loan in their name. All told, 34% have experienced at least one of these things in the past year.

data-leaks.prevalence: U.S. data compromises hit a record 3,322 in 2025 (Identity Theft Resource Center). 11% of Americans had an email or social media account taken over in the past year (Pew Research Center).

afraid-to-speak.name: Free speech
afraid-to-speak.line: I'm afraid to say what I really think.

sources.passage: Among the 65% who say in the survey they are fearful, they most often cited the threat of a violent response and fear of creating tension with friends and family.
But also censorship, for satisfying the need for protection, but for preventing satisfying the needs of understanding, participation and freedom.

afraid-to-speak.prevalence: 65% of Americans say they are fearful of consequences for speaking freely, most often a violent response or tension with friends and family (Freedom Forum).

press-freedom.name: Press freedom
press-freedom.line: I see reporters threatened, jailed or shut down for doing their jobs.

sources.passage: the global state of press freedom is now classified as a “difficult situation” for the first time in the history of the Index
Target 16.10 - In 2024, the number of killings of human rights defenders, journalists and trade unionists remained alarmingly high, with at least 502 cases reported across 44 countries
The survey also found Americans see a free press as the most threatened of the five freedoms under President Trump.

press-freedom.prevalence: In 2024 at least 502 killings of human rights defenders, journalists and trade unionists were reported across 44 countries (UN SDG 16.10 progress). RSF classed world press freedom as a "difficult situation" for the first time in the history of its index.

finding-help.name: Finding help
finding-help.line: I don't know what help is out there or where to ask for it.

sources.passage: In 2025, 211 community resource specialists made 19 million referrals for locally available help, 1 million more than in 2024
13 How available to you is the information you need in your daily life?

finding-help.prevalence: 211 made 19 million referrals for locally available help in 2025, 1 million more than in 2024 (United Way).

language-barriers.name: Language barriers
language-barriers.line: I can't get important information or services in a language I understand well.

sources.passage: Based on the 2019 data, 52% of people who spoke Chinese and 57% of those who spoke Vietnamese at home in the United States spoke English “less than very well,” compared to the other three common languages: Spanish 39%, Tagalog 30%, and Arabic 35%
The number of people in the United States who spoke a language other than English at home nearly tripled from 23.1 million (about 1 in 10) in 1980 to 67.8 million (almost 1 in 5) in 2019

language-barriers.prevalence: In 2019, 67.8 million people in the U.S. spoke a language other than English at home; 39% of Spanish speakers, 52% of Chinese speakers and 57% of Vietnamese speakers spoke English less than very well (U.S. Census Bureau).
